name: State Street Corporation

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Custody bank: holds and administers $59.2T of client assets (AUC/A) and runs $6.3T of investment funds (SSGA, SPDR ETFs); adds FX, securities lending and Charles River front-office software.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: 3Q26 revenue $4,004M: servicing fees $1,492M, management fees $797M, FX trading $427M, securities finance $151M, software $175M, other fees $98M, net interest income $864M; fees are 78% of revenue.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Asset owners, asset managers, insurers and pensions; 3Q26 wins $429B AUC/A mostly asset owners and managers. Some clients are competitors; 10-K gives no top-client percentage (nothing disclosed).

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: Non-US activities were $5,936M of $13,944M 2025 revenue (42.6%) and $95.7B of assets; dollar up 4.8% in 3 months hits translated fees, though NII is asset-sensitive in other currencies (+$285M per +100bp).

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Toll road on assets: servicing 10bp-ish of AUC/A (3Q26 annualised $1,492M x4 / $59.2T = 10.1bp vs 10.5bp a year ago) plus management fees (~50.6bp of AUM vs 48.8bp), plus spread on $271B of client deposits. Two-sentence model holds; revenue is market-linked, not contractual.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Operating leverage 531bp and pre-tax margin 34.6% (up 3.5 pts), expenses +8% vs revenue +13%; but half of costs are pay ($1,251M of $2,620M), capex $1,055M in 2025, and fees fall with markets while costs do not. Guidance raised in Oct (fees +13-14%, NII +15-16%, expenses +8-8.5%); outlook assumed equity markets flat from mid-Oct.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Inputs: skilled labour (48% of costs), technology and cloud vendors plus market-data and sub-custodian networks (supplier names and concentration not disclosed in the 10-K sections read), and client deposits as funding. Single point of failure: platform/operational outage, which the 10-K lists as a risk. Pass-through: fees are basis points on assets so inflation in costs is only recovered via repricing; the 10-K says pricing pressure is significant in custody and index management. Signal tags: equity levels and VIX (fees), fed_funds and 2y (NII +100bp = +$354M), dollar (translation, FX trading), wages (comp).

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Scale and switching costs: $59.2T custody book plus $2.98T AUC/A and $332M of servicing fees still to be installed; Charles River software ARR $442M (+8%), 3Q26 first Wealth Services mandate built on an existing Charles River client; SPDR ETF franchise (SPY inflows $68B ETF net in 3Q).

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Not a household name; SPDR (SPY, gold ETFs) is known to investors, but nobody outside finance would notice the custody business vanish. Management fee rate ~50bp of AUM vs low-cost index rivals; no consumer marketing line.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Rivals: BNY, JPMorgan, Northern Trust (custody); BlackRock, Vanguard (index funds). Servicing fee wins $68M in 3Q26; AUM +16% roughly tracks markets; Reported share data nothing found. Servicing fee rate slipped from 10.5bp to 10.1bp.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Install backlog $332M servicing fees; ARR +8%; Wealth Services entry; pending Santander CACEIS Latam purchase (subject to regulators); target ~$1B run-rate transformation benefit by 2029 (~$750M savings, ~$250M revenue). Software services revenue only +5% YoY, slower than ARR.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: ROTCE 25.1% (2025 about 18% on quoted averages) vs 10% cost of equity; CET1 11.0% (-0.3 pt YoY); $1.9B returned YTD (69% payout); common shares 288.7M to 272.8M in six quarters. Pay (DEF 14A) rewards three-year pre-tax margin and fee growth with ROE as a downward modifier. Insider ownership percentage not extracted. FCF not meaningful for a bank.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Custody is regulated, sticky and scale-driven; risks are fee compression in custody and index funds and being a service provider to competitors. Not losing relevance: AUC/A +15% YoY. Key-person risk modest (CEO O'Hanley; new Alpha president and COO named Sept 2026).

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 8-K Item 4.01 or 4.02, no NT filing, no CORRESP/UPLOAD in the filings list; auditor EY since 1972, one critical audit matter (servicing fee revenue), no material weakness. Soft flags: interim controller since Sept 2025 and a new CAO from Aug 2026; notable items in 2025 and 1Q26 (none in 3Q26).

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: good (asset-sensitive NII, fees up with markets). Slowdown: fees fall with equities, NII falls (-100bp = -$345M), offset by FX volatility and deposit inflows. 3Q26 FX volumes +31% in volatility. Markets fell about 7% since quarter-end while FY outlook assumed flat markets: 4Q fee risk.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Capital rules: CET1 11.0% with Basel/SCB set by the Fed; named in state AG antitrust litigation over coal/ESG; Santander CACEIS Latam purchase pending regulatory approvals. No dedicated docket pulled (deep dive item).

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $162.03 vs TBV/share $59.69 = 2.71x. At 10% cost of equity and 3% growth that implies lasting ROTCE of about 22% (20.3% at 4% growth) vs actual 25.1% in 3Q26 but about 18% for 2025, so cushion is thin and rests on a cycle-high ROTCE. P/E 13.2x on TTM EPS $12.25 vs year-end 2020-25 range 9.6x-13.4x (top of range). Peers: JPM 2.81x P/TBV and 13.3x P/E, BAC 1.67x, WFC 1.82x, GS 2.35x.

status_reason: Quality B and clean books, but at 2.71x TBV and 13.2x earnings the price assumes about 22% lasting ROTCE against about 18% last year and 25% now, and no clear mistake exists.

feedback.text: Servicing, management fees and FX volumes at records (FX client volume +31%, AUC/A +15%) confirm the hard-data Overheat read through Sept 30; the FY outlook assumed equity markets flat from mid-October, so the ~7% fall since is not in guidance (4Q fee risk).
feedback.effect: confirms overheat in hard data; markets signal slowdown risk

feedback.text: NII is asset-sensitive: +100bp parallel = +$354M, -100bp = -$345M over 12 months; average deposits $271B stable. A Fed hike helps, a slowdown with cuts hurts.
